evidence.ai_role: Evolutionary search changes doping-mask geometry to minimize VπL and doping-induced optical loss. The downstream neural-network application is motivation, not evidence of AI operation.
evidence.tested: CHARGE carrier simulations and MODE optical calculations evaluate the NSGA-II-selected doping geometry; INTERCONNECT simulates the converter.
evidence.unknown: No fabrication or independent experimental validation; representative-profile comparisons are source-reported and process assumptions constrain transfer.

source_review.scope: Primary full manuscript Methods, Results, validation protocol and limitations independently reviewed.

summary: A preprint used NSGA-II evolutionary optimization to vary doping-mask geometry and jointly reduce modulation voltage–length product and optical loss in a silicon microring junction. The resulting C-shaped profile reached a simulated VπL of about 0.39 V·cm, compared with 0.44–0.72 V·cm for representative profiles listed by the authors. Carrier and optical simulations fed a four-bit photonic converter model. These are computational device-design results under stated process assumptions; no fabricated junction, measured bandwidth or demonstrated neural-network acceleration was reported.
title: Evolutionary optimization designs a simulated low-voltage photonic junction
